decisions.reason: The unscoped MS15202P claim omits the 5.8L application and the catalog row carries a VIN-N restriction that the public vehicle context cannot enforce.
The unscoped 43186WT claim is cataloged for a different engine application than the article's 2.0L failure and covers only part of the article's years.
The unscoped Continental 40194 claim covers only the 1.9L application through 1996 and does not cover either 2.0L application or the full article range.
SKF BR930420 is a front 4WD hub application; the current unscoped two-vendor claim does not preserve the drivetrain and position restrictions needed for safe display.
The unscoped GN10237 row is cataloged for naturally aspirated applications and conflicts with the article's EcoBoost repair scope.
Walker 235-1027 carries VIN, production-date, and market restrictions that are not represented by the unscoped public claim.
The legacy 221-9025 row is unscoped and misses a 4.0L article year; the corrected packet introduces only the independently reviewed engine/year variants.
SKF BR930259K carries a bearing-identification restriction that is absent from the article and cannot be enforced by the current vehicle selection.
Bosch 0221504704 is unscoped across a broad F-150 year and engine range and lacks complete catalog coverage for the article.
MAHLE MS19261 is limited by engine, VIN, and year application while the existing public claim is unscoped.
MOOG 81118 has no complete catalog evidence for the article's vehicle scope, so the unscoped verified link cannot be retained.
SKF BR931016 is not supported across the article's full application set and the current unscoped row loses drivetrain and hub-option restrictions.
Bosch 6747 does not cover the article's 1998 endpoint and carries application variants that are absent from the unscoped claim.
Dayco DP2263 lacks catalog support for the article's 2021 endpoint, so the unscoped verified row is incomplete.
The Sachs K70564-01 claim conflicts with the DPS6 repair application and lacks the transmission-specific scope needed to distinguish it from manual and ST applications.
SKF BR930704 is a rear AWD application without the sensor configuration described by the article, while the existing row is unscoped and presented as a front repair.
The unscoped WPFD-609V row covers only a subset of the article's years and carries engine/application restrictions that are not enforced publicly.
The article describes six individual coil packs, while the catalog evidence identifies a different coil-pack configuration; the existing claim must remain blocked pending content correction.

Cardone 20-323 matches the prescribed power-steering pump, is catalog-confirmed for every 2005-2007 article year without an application restriction, and its existing exact eBay product link remains valid.
MAHLE MS16296 carries VIN, package, location, and application restrictions that are absent from the unscoped claim.
Cardone 47-1755 is a front-left window motor, but the article and existing row do not preserve the side and position restriction.
Aisin THRFD-0014 covers only a later/date-limited subset of the article, while the existing verified row is unscoped.
Denso 471-0919 is limited to 2019-2021 2.5L vehicles without rear climate control, restrictions the unscoped public claim does not preserve.
Delphi SS20881 is a rear-position sensor while the article instructs diagnosis of the affected corner; the unscoped row can expose the wrong position.
MAHLE MIS16230-1 misses the article's 1999 endpoint and carries a VIN/application restriction that is absent from the unscoped claim.
